terra.problem: Saying the fathers' sins 'came down' to the people adds an idea the verse does not state. They confess their sins and their fathers' iniquities.
The claim that gatherings like this often had offerings goes beyond the passage and has no reference.
Calling the moment quiet adds a detail the text does not give.
The passage does not say the crowd stays where it is. Also, standing is not the whole instruction: the Levites tell them to bless the LORD.
Saying the prayer takes the long way around 'on purpose' assigns an intention the text does not give.
Calling David Israel's king is a Bible fact from outside the passage, so it needs a reference.
Saying the Levites are reading Egypt's story out of the passage misrepresents them as reading this account rather than speaking in prayer.
Calling this 'the worst thing they did' ranks their actions in a way the text does not.
Clothes not wearing out does not establish that nothing needed fixing.
The passage says God multiplied their descendants like the stars, but it does not say He promised that comparison. The claim needs support from another referenced passage.
The statement that nobody drove them back out goes beyond what verse 24 says.
The verse describes houses full of goods, but it does not establish that nothing was picked clean.
Saying the prophets 'paid for' warning the people gives a reason for their deaths that the verse does not state.
Saying every baker is glad assumes a feeling the individual baker has not shared.
The verse says the abundant harvest goes to the kings, but does not say the people receive none of it.
The verse says the harvest goes to the kings, but does not specifically say the prophets receive none of it.
The agreement is put in writing, but the passage does not say it is written on paper.
